name: Hananiah the son of Azur
charge: Prophesying a lie in the name of the Lord, and breaking the yoke from off Jeremiah’s neck before the priests and all the people
summary: In the fourth year of Zedekiah, Hananiah the son of Azur, a prophet of Gibeon, told the priests and people in the Lord’s house that the Lord had broken the yoke of Babylon and would bring back the vessels, Jeconiah and the captives within two full years, and he broke the wooden yoke off Jeremiah’s neck (Jeremiah 28:1-4; Jeremiah 28:10-11). Jeremiah told him the Lord had not sent him, that he made the people trust in a lie and taught rebellion, and that he would die that year; he died in the seventh month (Jeremiah 28:15-17).
offenseFull: The Zedekiah teaching sets the climate: Jeconiah was still alive in Babylon and still revered as king, Zedekiah was known as a puppet, and a false hope was being spread that Jeconiah would soon return. The Lord had already told the people through Jeremiah that they would serve the king of Babylon seventy years (Jeremiah 25:11-12), and had Jeremiah wear a yoke as the sign that the nations must bring their necks under Babylon’s yoke (Jeremiah 27:2; Jeremiah 27:12).

Into that setting Hananiah, a so-called prophet of Gibeon, as the study note calls him, stood in the house of the Lord before the priests and all the people and said the Lord had broken the yoke of the king of Babylon, and within two full years would bring back the vessels of the Lord’s house, Jeconiah and all the captives (Jeremiah 28:1-4). The Hammertime class, whose theme is forefathers whose sins cursed their seed, sets his two years against the seventy the people had already been given: they understood the prophecy was going to be seventy years. It was prosperity, peace, peace, the teacher says, and there was no peace (Jeremiah 23:16-17; Jeremiah 6:14). He said thus says the Lord when the Lord had told him nothing, the Zedekiah teaching says, taking the Lord’s name in vain (Exodus 20:7).

Jeremiah said amen, may the Lord do so, but told him not to hold on to it: the prophets of old prophesied war, evil and pestilence against many countries, and a prophet who prophesies peace is known to be sent by the Lord only when his word comes to pass (Jeremiah 28:5-9). The class of 2026-04-11 says the war and pestilence the old prophets foretold is what you see our leadership doing today, and they will be made known when the mission is accomplished. Hananiah then took the yoke off Jeremiah’s neck and broke it before the people, saying the Lord would break Nebuchadnezzar’s yoke from all nations within two years, and Jeremiah went his way (Jeremiah 28:10-11). Jeremiah got on him, one class says, for teaching peace and safety; the prophets of the Lord come teaching that evil is coming, and the feel-good preachers are the opposite. Your pastor, another teacher says, is still telling you it is your season.
judgmentFull: The word came to Jeremiah: Hananiah had broken yokes of wood, but in their place he would make yokes of iron; the Lord had put an iron yoke on the neck of all these nations to serve Nebuchadnezzar, and had given him even the beasts of the field (Jeremiah 28:12-14). Babylon was the superpower at that time, the study note says. The Zedekiah teaching reads the yoke as vassal service and taxation to Babylon, not chattel slavery; another teaching sets the yoke of iron beside the iron yoke of the curses (Deuteronomy 28:48), which it carries forward to the chains of the later captivity. Then Jeremiah told Hananiah the Lord had not sent him, that he made this people trust in a lie, and that the Lord would cast him off the face of the earth: that year he would die, because he had taught rebellion against the Lord (Jeremiah 28:15-16). The study note explains the rebellion: he taught the people to go against the Most High instead of accepting that they had to go through captivity. Hananiah died the same year, in the seventh month (Jeremiah 28:17).

The law had already set the sentence: the prophet who presumes to speak a word in the Lord’s name that He did not command shall die, and the sign is that the thing does not come to pass (Deuteronomy 18:20-22). By this law, the study note says, a lot of these pastors stand condemned, who claim Christ said what He never said. These false pastors make our people trust in lies, one teacher says; we are not here to spread peace on the earth but to prophesy against many nations. The Hammertime class shows what one man can do: it takes just one, like Theudas and Judas of Galilee, who drew people after them and perished (Acts 5:36-37), and it warns against those who corrupt the word of God (2 Corinthians 2:17) and against presumptuous sins (Psalm 19:13).

lawsResolved.text: Lying pastors and those that withhold the truth of God's word are cursed for causing national apostasy.
You shall not bear false witness against another nor raise a false report.
You are not to take the name of God in vain.
Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.

text.text: And it came to pass the same year, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fourth year, and in the fifth month, that Hananiah the son of Azur the prophet, which was of Gibeon, spake unto me in the house of the Lord, in the presence of the priests and of all the people, saying,
Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, saying, I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Within two full years will I bring again into this place all the vessels of the Lord’s house, that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took away from this place, and carried them to Babylon:

And I will bring again to this place Jeconiah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, with all the captives of Judah, that went into Babylon, saith the Lord: for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Then Hananiah the prophet took the yoke from off the prophet Jeremiah’s neck, and brake it.

And Hananiah spake in the presence of all the people, saying, Thus saith the Lord; Even so will I break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all nations within the space of two full years. And the prophet Jeremiah went his way.
Then said the prophet Jeremiah unto Hananiah the prophet, Hear now, Hananiah; The Lord hath not sent thee; but thou makest this people to trust in a lie.
Therefore thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will cast thee from off the face of the earth: this year thou shalt die, because thou hast taught rebellion against the Lord.
So Hananiah the prophet died the same year in the seventh month.
And this whole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.

And it shall come to pass, when seventy years are accomplished, that I will punish the king of Babylon, and that nation, saith the Lord, for their iniquity, and the land of the Chaldeans, and will make it perpetual desolations.
Thus saith the Lord to me; Make thee bonds and yokes, and put them upon thy neck,
I spake also to Zedekiah king of Judah according to all these words, saying, Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and live.
Thus saith the Lord of hosts, Hearken not unto the words of the prophets that prophesy unto you: they make you vain: they speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of the Lord.
They say still unto them that despise me, The Lord hath said, Ye shall have peace; and they say unto every one that walketh after the imagination of his own heart, No evil shall come upon you.
They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace.
Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.
Then the prophet Jeremiah said unto the prophet Hananiah in the presence of the priests, and in the presence of all the people that stood in the house of the Lord,

Even the prophet Jeremiah said, Amen: the Lord do so: the Lord perform thy words which thou hast prophesied, to bring again the vessels of the Lord’s house, and all that is carried away captive, from Babylon into this place.
Nevertheless hear thou now this word that I speak in thine ears, and in the ears of all the people;
The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied both against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.
The prophet which prophesieth of peace, when the word of the prophet shall come to pass, then shall the prophet be known, that the Lord hath truly sent him.
Then the word of the Lord came unto Jeremiah the prophet, after that Hananiah the prophet had broken the yoke from off the neck of the prophet Jeremiah, saying,
Go and tell Hananiah, saying, Thus saith the Lord; Thou hast broken the yokes of wood; but thou shalt make for them yokes of iron.

For thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; I have put a yoke of iron upon the neck of all these nations, that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon; and they shall serve him: and I have given him the beasts of the field also.

Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things: and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.
Then said the prophet Jeremiah unto Hananiah the prophet, Hear now, Hananiah; The Lord hath not sent thee; but thou makest this people to trust in a lie.
Therefore thus saith the Lord; Behold, I will cast thee from off the face of the earth: this year thou shalt die, because thou hast taught rebellion against the Lord.
So Hananiah the prophet died the same year in the seventh month.
But the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die.
And if thou say in thine heart, How shall we know the word which the Lord hath not spoken?

When a prophet speaketh in the name of the Lord, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the Lord hath not spoken, but the prophet hath spoken it presumptuously: thou shalt not be afraid of him.

For before these days rose up Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody; to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves: who was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to nought.
After this man rose up Judas of Galilee in the days of the taxing, and drew away much people after him: he also perished; and all, even as many as obeyed him, were dispersed.
For we are not as many, which corrupt the word of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God speak we in Christ.
Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins; let them not have dominion over me: then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the great transgression.
